text: Route prefix: /philhealth. Manages PhilHealth - the Philippine Health Insurance Corporation - membership, claims, form generation, batch processing, and reporting. All PhilHealth operations require permission: philhealth.view (basic) or philhealth.manage (claims/batches/pdfs).

Route: philhealth.icd10-codes (permission: philhealth.view). ICD-10 diagnosis codes catalog. The WHO International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision. Used in PhilHealth claims for diagnosis coding. Fields: id, icd10_code (e.g. 'A00', 'J06.9', 'I10', 'K35'), icd10_description (e.g. 'Cholera', 'Acute upper respiratory infection, unspecified', 'Essential (primary) hypertension', 'Acute appendicitis'), chapter (e.g. 'I - Certain infectious and parasitic diseases'), block, is_active, tenant_id, history, audit columns. ICD10 codes are linked to diagnoses in EMR encounters and used in claim forms (CF1-CF5) for primary and secondary diagnoses.

Route: philhealth.rvs-codes (permission: philhealth.view). PhilHealth RVS codes - the standardized fee schedule codes for medical services. Each RVS code maps a service to its PhilHealth-recognised fee. Fields: id, rvs_code, service_description, service_category (e.g. 'Physician Service', 'Laboratory', 'Radiology', 'Drug/Pharma', 'Surgical Package', 'Professional Fee'), rvs_point_value (or fee amount), is_active, tenant_id, history, audit columns. RVS codes are used in PhilHealth claim forms to itemize services for reimbursement.

Route: philhealth.case-rates (permission: philhealth.view). PhilHealth case rate schedules - fixed-rate packages for specific clinical conditions/procedures. Fields: id, case_rate_code, case_description, package_type (e.g. 'Normal Delivery', 'Cesarean Section', 'Hemorrhage', 'Pneumonia - Pneumococcal', 'Stroke', 'CABG', 'Hip Replacement', 'Kidney Transplant'), case_rate_amount (fixed fee), coverage_duration_days (e.g. 3 days, 5 days, etc.), is_active, tenant_id, history, audit columns. Case rates are used for cashless/emergency admissions under PhilHealth's Z-benefit / Case Rate program.

Route: philhealth.hc-professionals (permission: philhealth.view). Healthcare professional registry for PhilHealth purposes. Fields: id, hc_professional_id (FK to health_care_professionals.id), philhealth_prc_no (PRC license number), philhealth_id (PhilHealth provider ID), profession (Physician, Dentist, Nurse, Medical Technologist, Radiologic Technologist, Pharmacist, etc.), specialization, is_active, tenant_id, history, audit columns. HC professionals used as service providers in PhilHealth claims must be registered here.

Route: philhealth.members (permission: philhealth.view). PhilHealth membership records. This is what links a patient to their PhilHealth membership for claims eligibility. Fields: id, philhealth_member_id (the PhilHealth membership number - this is what the patient. philhealth_member_id FK points to), last_name, first_name, middle_name, suffix, date_of_birth, sex, address_street, barangay_id, city_id, province_id, region_id, membership_type (Individual Payor, Employer-Employed, Employer-Voluntary, Overseas Filipino Worker (OFW), Indigent/Sponsored, Lifetime Member, etc.), membership_status (Active, Inactive, Cancelled, Expired, Pending), enrollment_date, benefit_rating, is_active, tenant_id, history, audit columns.

items: The Patient model has a philhealth_member_id FK that points to this table. When filling out patient registration, if is_philhealth_member is checked, the user selects an existing PhilHealth member record.
If the patient's PhilHealth membership does not exist yet, create it here first under PhilHealth > Members.
PhilHealth membership status must be 'Active' for the patient to be eligible for PhilHealth claims.

text: Route: philhealth.claims (permission: philhealth.manage). PhilHealth claim management - the core claims workflow. Claims are requests for PhilHealth reimbursement for medical services rendered to accredited members.

items: id - Primary key.
tenant_id - FK to hospitals.id.
claim_code - Code: 'PH-' + 5-digit sequence (e.g. PH-00001, PH-00002).
philhealth_member_id - FK to philhealth_members.id. The patient's PhilHealth membership.
patient_id - FK to patients.id. (Redundant but useful for easy lookup.)
claim_type - String: 'Outpatient', 'Inpatient', 'Emergency', 'Maternity', 'Z-Benefit/Case Rate', 'Konsulta', 'HMO Referral', etc.
admission_id - FK to admissions.id (for inpatient claims; nullable for outpatient).
opd_consultation_id - FK to opd_consultations.id (for outpatient/diagnostic claims; nullable).
service_date - Date. Date the service was rendered.
facility_id - String. PhilHealth-accredited facility code (the hospital's PhilHealth accreditation number).
diagnosis_primary_id - FK to icd10_codes.id. Primary diagnosis (ICD10 code).
diagnosis_secondary_id - FK to icd10_codes.id (nullable). Secondary diagnosis.
diagnosis_tertiary_id - FK to icd10_codes.id (nullable). Tertiary diagnosis.
total_claim_amount - Float. Total amount claimed for PhilHealth reimbursement.
philhealth_reimbursement - Float. Amount PhilHealth approved/reimbursed (set after claim is processed by PhilHealth).
patient_share - Float. Patient's share/co-pay (if any).
hospital_share - Float. Hospital's share (total - reimbursement - patient_share).
status - Claim status: Draft, Submitted, Pending Review, Approved, Disapproved/Rejected, Paid, Adjusted, Closed.
submission_date - Date (nullable). When the claim was submitted to PhilHealth.
philhealth_ref_no - String (nullable). PhilHealth's reference number for the claim.
remarks - Text (nullable).
created_by / created_date - Audit columns.
updated_by / updated_date - Audit columns.
history - Soft delete flag (1=active).
is_active - Active flag.
id - Primary key.
philhealth_claim_id - FK to philhealth_claims.id.

service_type - String: 'Physician Service', 'Laboratory', 'Radiology', 'Drug/Pharmaceutical', 'Surgical Package', 'Professional Fee', 'Nursing Service', 'Blood Transfusion', 'Isolation Room', 'Intensive Care', 'Burn Care', etc.
service_description - String. Description of the service/item.
quantity - Float. Quantity of service (e.g. 1 for physician professional fee, number of lab tests, number of drug days, etc.).
rvs_code - FK to philhealth_rvs_codes.id (nullable). The PhilHealth RVS code for this service (if applicable).
case_rate_code - FK to philhealth_case_rates.id (nullable). The case rate package (if claim is a case rate / Z-benefit).
unit_rate - Float. Rate per unit of service.
total_amount - Float. Quantity x unit_rate. The claimed amount for this line item.
philhealth_allowed - Float (nullable). Amount PhilHealth allows/covered for this service (after deduction).
patient_share_amount - Float (nullable). Patient's co-pay for this item.
sequence - Int. Sequence number for the line item in the claim form.
is_active - Active flag.
history - Soft delete flag.
From the PhilHealth claims page, create a new claim.
Select PhilHealth member (or search patient - links to existing membership).
Set claim_type: Outpatient, Inpatient, Emergency, Maternity, Z-Benefit/Case Rate, Konsulta, HMO Referral.
Link to the encounter: for inpatient, link to admission_id. For outpatient, link to opd_consultation_id.
Set service_date.
Enter primary diagnosis (ICD10 code from philhealth.icd10-codes master).
Optionally enter secondary and tertiary diagnoses.
Add claim services/line items: each line item has service_type, description, quantity, rvs_code (if applicable), unit_rate, total_amount.
For case rate claims: select the case_rate_code, and the system populates the case_rate_amount and coverage duration.
System computes total_claim_amount (sum of all line items).
Review the claim, then submit. Status becomes 'Submitted' (or 'Pending Review' if internal review required before submission).
When PhilHealth processes and approves: update status to 'Approved', enter philhealth_ref_no, philhealth_reimbursement amount, patient_share, hospital_share.
When paid: status becomes 'Paid'.
If rejected/disapproved: status becomes 'Disapproved/Rejected' with reason in remarks.
The claim lifecycle: Draft -> Submitted -> Pending Review -> Approved/Paid OR Disapproved.

philhealth.batches - Group claims into batches for submission. A batch is a collection of claims submitted together to PhilHealth. Useful for organizing claims by submission period (weekly/monthly). Fields: id, batch_code (e.g. 'BATCH-2026-09'), description, total_claims, total_amount, submitted_date, philhealth_batch_ref, status.
philhealth.reports - PhilHealth reports: claims summary by claim type, claims by diagnosis (ICD10), claims by facility, claims aging, reimbursement summary, batch listing, claim line item report.

text: These routes generate official PhilHealth claim forms as downloadable PDFs via DomPDF. Each form is a standardized PhilHealth document:

items: philhealth.claims.esoapdf ({claim}) - PhilHealth E-SOAP (Electronic Summary of Accounts and Payments) PDF. Shows the complete claim with all services, amounts, and the computed E-SOAP. The digital equivalent of the traditional PhilHealth claim form.

philhealth.claims.cf1pdf ({claim}) - PhilHealth CF1 (Claim Form 1) PDF. The CF1 form lists the patient's demographic and insurance information, the admitting facility, the primary/secondary/tertiary diagnoses (ICD10), the attending physician details, and the hospitalization summary.

philhealth.claims.cf2pdf ({claim}) - PhilHealth CF2 (Claim Form 2) PDF. The CF2 form itemizes all services rendered with their RVS codes (if applicable), quantities, unit rates, total amounts, PhilHealth allowed amounts, and patient shares. This is the detailed service breakdown.

philhealth.claims.cf3pdf ({claim}) - PhilHealth CF3 (Claim Form 3) PDF. The CF3 form lists the medications/pharmaceuticals administered during the admission, with drug names, dosages, quantities, and charges.
philhealth.claims.cf4pdf ({claim}) - PhilHealth CF4 (Claim Form 4) PDF. The CF4 form lists laboratory tests performed, with test names, results (if relevant), RVS codes, charges, and amounts.

philhealth.claims.cf5pdf ({claim}) - PhilHealth CF5 (Claim Form 5) PDF. The CF5 form lists radiology/imaging procedures performed, with exam types, modalities, findings summary, RVS codes, charges, and amounts.

philhealth.claims.eeclpdf ({claim}) - PhilHealth EECL (Emergency Encounter Closure List) PDF. For emergency admissions, the EECL form documents the emergency encounter with triage level, OECB package (if applicable), diagnosis, and disposition. This is the emergency equivalent of the inpatient claim summary.

text: These PDFs are the official PhilHealth submission documents. Hospitals submit these forms (electronically or physically) to PhilHealth for reimbursement.

Route: /medical-records (permission: medical-records.view). Manages medical certificate generation and patient chart access. This is the official records module - the legal medical documentation output.

The medical records module generates various medical certificates as PDFs via DomPDF. These are official medical documents used for employment, schooling, legal purposes, insurance, and government requirements.

items: Medical Certificate (MC) - General medical certificate stating the patient's condition, date of examination, fitness status (fit to work, unfit for work, fit with restrictions), recommended rest period, and physician signature block. Generated from patient encounters.
Certificate of Employment (COE) - Certificate verifying the patient's employment status (if employer provided), used for employment verification.

Certificate of Disability (COD) - Certificate documenting the patient's disability status, disability type, degree of disability, and recommendations. Used for PWD ID application, government benefits, and accommodations.
Nil per os (NPO) Order / Special Orders - Hospital orders: NPO (nothing by mouth), activity orders (bed rest, ambulate as tolerated, etc.), diet orders, positioning orders, monitoring orders.
Letter of Request / Referral Letter - Letter from the attending physician to another facility/specialist requesting referral, consultation, or transfer.
Fit to Work / Fit to Fly / Fit to Travel Certificate - Certificate clearing the patient for specific activities.
Encashment / Reimbursement Certificate - For HMO/insurance claims documentation.
Birth Certificate / Delivery Note - For delivery patients: details of delivery, mother and baby information, attending physicians, delivery type, complications, Apgar score (if newborn), etc.
Death Certificate - For expired patients: patient details, cause of death (primary and underlying), time of death, attending physician certification.
All certificates are generated server-side via Barryvdh DomPDF.
Templates use Blade templates rendered to HTML, then converted to PDF.
Certificate data is pulled from the patient record and associated encounters (OPD consultations, ER admissions, admissions, delivery records, etc.).
The patient's demographic data (name, age, sex, address) comes from the Patient model.
The clinical information (diagnosis, findings, treatment) comes from the encounter records.
The physician's name and signature block come from the attending physician (health_care_professionals) and the user who generated the certificate.
Generated PDFs are downloadable and printable.
The certificate generation interface shows available certificate types, lets the user select the patient and encounter, fills in certificate-specific fields, and generates the PDF.

text: The patient chart (see also 4.6) is accessible from medical records. It shows the patient's complete medical record across all encounters and modules. From medical-records.view permission, the chart shows: demographics, all OPD consultations with SOAP notes and orders, all ER admissions with triage and treatment, all inpatient admissions with ward/ICU/OR course, all lab requests and results, all radiology requests and reports, all pharmacy requests and dispensing history (PMR), all CSR requests and dispensing, all procedure orders, all billing invoices and payments, PhilHealth membership and claims, and all certificates generated. The patient chart is the single comprehensive view of the patient's health record.
